translations.answer: The maintainer separated the two parts: the stiffness term from the tendon length exceeding the spring-length interval, and the damping term related to tendon velocity; the limit constraint force was read from sensor/tendonlimitfrc. The total force is obtained by summing the two parts. The official engine_passive.c provides the spring/damper implementation, and the XML reference explicitly states that tendonlimitfrc is the tendon limit constraint force sensor. The original thread user confirmed that the passive spring force calculation is effective for their model. The local variable frc_spring should not be considered as an external API.
translations.applicability: This applies to MuJoCo models that include both passive tendon spring/damper and tendon limit constraint. Only the corresponding force component should be retained when only one is present.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. It has been formally documented or independently reproducible with precise reference.
translations.details.attempts.0: A free mounting body is used as the tendon attachment point, and it is welded to the target body to measure the weld force.
translations.details.attempts.1: A user adjusted the weld solref to 0.00021, reporting that the elongation was only partially improved.
translations.details.attempts.2: The passive force and tendonlimitfrc are calculated separately according to the maintainer's final suggestion.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, distinguish between the passive spring/damper force and the tendon limit constraint force, and do not sum a zero-value site sensor as the total.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compare the tendon spring/damper calculation in engine_passive.c with the XML reference for tendonlimitfrc constraint force definition.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: If using a welded mounting body, check the mass, weld softness, and tendon elongation.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: For the passive force, calculate according to the official engine source code's tendon spring/damper definition; for the constraint force, use sensor/tendonlimitfrc; sum the two when total force is required.
translations.details.environments.0: MuJoCo public Issue #832, 2023–2025 reply; passive tendon, tendon limit constraint, and site/weld force sensor.
translations.details.environments.1: The official source code locates this in commit 100b1a06fd8f6a184a3e495adff3ff044b1ff4f2, lines 377–415 of engine_passive.c.
translations.details.limits.0: frc_spring is a local calculation variable in the engine source code and should not be rewritten as a stable, public API name.
translations.details.limits.1: tendonlimitfrc only represents the tendon limit constraint force and does not automatically include the passive spring and damping forces.
translations.details.limits.2: The welded mounting body workaround has not been verified by the maintainer and there are known deviations in mass, weld softness, and tendon elongation.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original thread user confirmed that the passive spring force calculation is effective for their model.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The site sensor gap in the engine for tendon force has not been marked as fixed in this Issue.
translations.details.outcomes.2: The welded mounting-body workaround results in conflicting data across different users.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why is the force sensor at the tendon attachment point not returning the tendon force?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How can we separately obtain the passive tendon force, the tendon limit constraint force, and the total force?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Is the measurement of tendon force via a welded mounting body reliable?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before using simulation tendon force in real machines or for safety protection, apply known load calibration to the passive force, constraint force, and sensor sign independently.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The project collaborator confirmed that the site force sensor at the time of implementation missed the tendon force and referred to it as a gap/defect.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The error in the welded workaround is related to the mounting body mass, weld softness, and the constraint of the mounting body, but the original thread did not provide a general error model.
translations.details.symptoms.0: When there is force on the tendon, the force sensor at the attachment point still reads zero.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The welded mounting-body workaround causes elongation and force deviation in some models.
translations.source.locator: Issue #832, maintainer's decomposition method in the issuecomment-3148619744; user confirmation in issuecomment-3152635424; official source code 377–415 lines of engine_passive.c and XML tendonlimitfrc document.
